Finally, we train the model on data preprocessed with optimal-transport alignment, which guarantees a well-defined mapping between control and perturbed samples and further stabilizes the learned latent representations. We demonstrate that RAPTORGraph improves state-of-the-art performance on downstream analyses of unseen perturbations, such as non-additive interactions, while performing competitively on objective metrics, such as mean squared error and maximum mean discrepancy. The source code is available at https://github.com/sXperfect/RAPTORGraph.

items.title: Transmural Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Nominates Candidate Disease Programs in Human Necrotizing Enterocolitis
items.abstract_or_text: Background & Aims: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening disease of premature infants marked by inflammation, ischemia, mucosal injury, and, in advanced cases, necrosis extending into deeper layers of the intestinal wall. Because NEC affects specialized, interacting cells in a developing intestine, we used single-nucleus transcriptomics to build a transmural, cell-type-resolved map and nominate hypothesis-generating disease programs distinct from maturation. Methods: Full-thickness intestinal specimens from fetal/prenatal controls, acute NEC cases, and infant controls were analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq). Fetal and infant samples served as developmental references. Analyses included cell annotation, NEC-versus-infant differential expression, gene ontology (GO), cross-lineage recurrence, cell death signatures, and developmental maturity. Results: We profiled 53,735 nuclei by snRNA-seq and resolved 34 epithelial, stromal, vascular, immune, neuronal, glial, and smooth muscle populations. We used a morphology-based nuclei scoring system for sample selection that predicted high-quality transcript recovery. NEC nuclei were represented across this cellular landscape, with recurrent gene-expression changes suggesting shared inflammatory recruitment, antimicrobial/redox defense, stress adaptation, complement/vascular activation, reduced homeostatic signaling, and cell death-associated regulation. Developmental maturity analysis identified fetal-like expression levels in subsets of NEC-regulated genes. Proliferative crypt populations retained DNA repair/cell-cycle programs with inflammatory, hypoxic, and ER-stress features, while absorptive enterocytes showed reduced digestive, transport, detoxification, and terminal villus-function programs. Secretory-lineage changes implicated goblet mucus-barrier responses with reduced glycosylation, trafficking, and hydration; enteroendocrine changes in epithelial defense, metabolic stress, and neural signaling; and Paneth cell retention of antimicrobial effector transcripts despite altered ER quality control, autophagy, and granule delivery in NEC. Non-epithelial programs implicated stromal Wnt/BMP niche loss, impaired lymphatic drainage/scavenging, macrophage cytokine activation with reduced clearance machinery, neuroglial circuit defects, and altered smooth muscle contraction-relaxation balance. Conclusions: This single nuclear intestinal cell atlas nominates multicellular programs that may govern NEC initiation, progression toward tissue destruction, and resolution toward functional recovery.

items.title: Micro-fragmented adipose tissue reprogrammes the systemic molecular landscape of inflammatory knee osteoarthritis
items.abstract_or_text: Knee osteoarthritis affects an estimated 374 million people and has no approved disease-modifying treatment. In our double-blind randomised trial (ISRCTN88966184), intra-articular micro-fragmented adipose tissue (MFAT) outperformed hyaluronic acid (HA) on pain, function and cartilage composition, but clinical endpoints alone cannot say whether the disease changed or only the symptoms. Here we answer that question from the blood. Using an interpretable AI data-fusion framework based on non-negative matrix tri-factorisation, we integrated longitudinal plasma proteomics, N-glycomics and miRNA transcriptomics with patient genetics and prior molecular networks at baseline, one and six months, resolving 93 gene and 30 miRNA pathways, almost all significantly enriched in Gene Ontology Biological Process and Reactome annotations. By six months the two injections had left sharply distinct molecular fingerprints. HA remained dominated by canonical OA pathogenesis, including the cartilage-degrading effectors MMP13 and LIMK2 and persistent markers of synovial inflammation. MFAT instead shifted the systemic landscape towards chondroprotection, anti-inflammatory signalling and bone-cartilage homeostasis, prioritising effectors including SIRT7 and NDUFC1. These are, to our knowledge, the first in vivo human data to explain why a regenerative therapy outperforms viscosupplementation in knee osteoarthritis, and they place MFAT on the disease-modifying rather than the symptomatic side of that divide.

items.title: Characterization of the frameshift c.515dupC knock-in mouse model of HSPB8-associated myopathy (MFM13) and evaluation of Trehalose as autophagy modulating therapy.
items.abstract_or_text: Heat shock protein family B member 8 (HSPB8) is a chaperone involved in the chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA) complex. HSPB8 in conjunction with cochaperone Bcl2-associated athanogene 3 (BAG3), promotes autophagy-mediated removal of misfolded proteins associated with various neurodegenerative diseases. Mutations in HSPB8, previously associated with Charcot Marie Tooth disease type 2L, have recently been linked to an autosomal dominant rimmed vacuolar myopathy (MFM13), and is considered a multisystem proteinopathy. Patients have distal and proximal limb girdle myopathy with muscle biopsy showing fatty replacement, endomysial fibrosis, and rimmed vacuoles leading to muscle atrophy and early demise. We have demonstrated reduced expression of HSPB8, altered autophagy, and TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) accumulation in patient fibroblasts. Overexpressed murine Hspb8 frameshift mutant (c.515dupC, fs) displays insolubility and aggregation propensity in Murine Neuroblastoma X Spinal Cord 34 (NSC-34) cells. Using clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) technology, we generated a knock-in Hspb8 mouse model of the c.515dupC hot spot frameshift variant to study disease pathology. Mutant Hspb8 mice developed late onset muscle weakness beginning at 15 months. Muscle biochemical analyses revealed reduced HSPB8 levels, increased TDP 43, and altered autophagy markers, partially recapitulating the human phenotype. Fiber type analysis, neuromuscular junction integrity, and motor neurons show mild myopathy without neurodegeneration. Given the lack of available treatments, we evaluated trehalose, a natural disaccharide that is known to induce HSPB8 and enhance autophagy as a potential therapy. Administration of 2% trehalose in the drinking water restored HSPB8 expression; however, it did not significantly ameliorate autophagic dysfunction or TDP-43 pathology in mutant mice. These findings support the value of our preclinical models for translational studies, and autophagy enhancement as a potential therapeutic strategy for HSPB8-related myopathy.

items.title: AI-Based MRI Radiomics for Preoperative Detection of Tumor Deposits in Rectal Cancer: A Bivariate Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA). Databases were screened for DTA studies of MRI-based radiomics predicting TDs in adult RC patients with histopathology as reference. Results: Nine studies (2589 patients) were identified. Across included studies, the bivariate meta-analysis showed pooled sensitivity of 0.765 (95% CI 0.714 - 0.809) and specificity of 0.790 (95% CI 0.750 - 0.825), with overall AUC of 0.845 and very low heterogeneity (I2 = 7.3%). In validation datasets, diagnostic performance remained consistent (AUC 0.806), with pooled sensitivity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809) and specificity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809). For MRI modality, T2 weighted image (T2WI) showed higher sensitivity (0.745) than T2WI plus diffusion weighted image (DWI) (0.697), while T2WI+DWI had higher specificity (0.809 vs 0.737) and AUC (0.829 vs 0.796), with no significant subgroup differences (p[≥]0.192). Models combining radiomics with clinical/radiological variables achieved significantly higher sensitivity (0.842 vs 0.657, p<0.001) and higher AUC (0.827 vs 0.752), with comparable specificity. Conclusion: MRI-based radiomics demonstrates good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in RC. The integration of radiomics with clinical or imaging features increases the accuracy of identification. Amongst the MRI modalities, models that utilize the combination of T2WI plus DWI are more accurate than those using T2WI or DWI only.

items.title: Matched-Control Benchmarking of Quantum Machine Learning Models for Hierarchical Protein Function Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Predicting protein function requires assigning hierarchical Gene Ontology (GO) terms to sequences with limited experimental annotation. We tested whether quantum machine learning improves this task when each model is compared with a classical control matched to its architecture or input representation. Five quantum models spanning variational circuits, quantum features, and fidelity kernels were evaluated on 40,000 proteins from the CAFA6 training release, using frozen 480-dimensional ESM-2 embeddings, 180 GO terms, and an internal cluster-disjoint train–validation–test split. Kernel bandwidths were selected through a training-only concentration screen (Gate-0), which also estimated shots required per kernel entry. Across five seeds, the standalone quantum models scored below their matched controls by 0.0023–0.0847 in aspect-mean maximum F-measure; the 48-layer re-uploading kernel was admitted in only two seeds and lost in both. Freezing the variational circuit did not reduce performance. Late fusion of quantum and classical predictions improved on cosine nearest neighbours by 0.0034, but kernel-level mixing selected a purely classical weight, and the fused score (0.6697) remained below that of a classical RBF nearest-neighbour model (0.6719). Finite-shot simulations preserved this ordering, although the quantum kernel ridge model was sensitive to shot noise. These results provide no evidence of a standalone quantum advantage on this benchmark. The fusion gain is consistent with complementary prediction errors, but its mechanism remains to be tested against a matched classical ensemble.

items.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals PITX1 as a predictor of immunotherapy efficacy in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but predictive biomarkers are lacking. The role of paired-like homeodomain 1 (PITX1) in ccRCC remains unclear. Methods Machine learning identified PITX1 as a key biomarker. Multi-omics analyses integrated bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics (ST), data from three randomized controlled trials (IMmotion151, CheckMate025, JAVELIN Renal 101) and West China Hospital ccRCC cohort. Results PITX1 was upregulated in ccRCC, associated with BAP1 mutation and hypomethylation. scRNA-seq and ST revealed the expression patterns of PITX1 in different cell clusters. High PITX1 expression correlated with advanced clinicopathological features, poor survival, and metabolic reprogramming towards glucose and methionine metabolism. Enrichment analysis suggested high PITX1 would lead to more malignant tumor biological behaviors. It shaped an immunosuppressive microenvironment with regulatory T cells (Tregs) infiltrated and elevated immune checkpoints. Crucially, high PITX1 indicates inferior benefits for patients receiving immunotherapy. Conclusion PITX1 is a novel biomarker linked to aggressive tumor behavior, metabolic alteration, and immune evasion, predicting poor response to immunotherapy in ccRCC.

items.title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks
items.abstract_or_text: Understanding how neurons respond to visual stimulus is an important question in both deep learning and neuroscience. It has significant implications for enhancing the interpretability of black-box artificial neural networks and for understanding the visual representation in the human brain. We propose a structured visual representations landscape and design an activation-based prior that allows us to effectively regularize the landscape with activations from brain regions or neural network units. Our model Vis-Lens integrates a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model into an image generation framework. It enables the generation of natural, realistic preferred images by directly modifying the activation-regularized latent codes without per-image iterative optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on both artificial neural networks and human visual cortex using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. Our framework improves activation modulation and image realism compared with a recent state-of-the-art method for generating preferred visual representations of these neural targets.

items.title: Attribution-based diagnostics for single-cell foundation models
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell RNA foundation models (scFMs) are increasingly used for in-silico biological discovery, yet predictive performance alone does not reveal whether their decisions rely on biologically meaningful signals or model-specific shortcuts. We systematically investigate post-hoc attribution of downstream predictions across two tasks: cell-type annotation using pretrained Cell2Sentence and scGPT models, and perturbation prediction using scGPT+STATE in a controlled setting. For cell annotation, we use attribution to assess whether predictions rely on established marker genes and how their relevance varies with model architecture, expression rank, and the surrounding cellular context. For perturbation prediction, we compare attribution patterns with known regulatory ground-truth in a synthetic setting to assess what they reveal about the model's learned computations. Across these tasks, attribution reveals biological feature use, contextual interactions, contributions from different input pathways, learning progression, associations with prediction quality, and potential pitfalls that are not fully captured by standard performance metrics. Experiments with complete and limited regulatory knowledge further demonstrate that conclusions drawn from attribution depend strongly on the choice of biological reference, baseline, and null model. Together, these findings highlight the value of attribution as a flexible post-hoc diagnostic for understanding model behavior, identifying potential issues, and informing the development of scFMs.

items.title: A decision-only model as a low-cost judge of medical AI answers
items.abstract_or_text: Background. Testing and deploying medical AI systems at scale already results in more outputs than clinicians can review, and the use of large language models (LLMs) as judges is growing rapidly. Decision-only models, cheap and fast models that return structured probabilities rather than text, offer a potentially scalable option for that goal. Methods. In an OSF pre-registered evaluation, we tested TypeSafe Jev 1.13 as a judge on tasks from five validated clinical benchmarks: rubric grading (HealthBench), planted clinical errors (When Rubrics Fail), risk in AI-written clinical documents (MedVAL), counseling ratings and failures (CounselBench) and physicians' preferences between answers (Real-POCQi). Comparators were expert raters' agreement with each other, OpenAI Decisions, GPT-6 Luna, a proposed hybrid team combining decision models and a cheap LLM and, as frontier comparators, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. The main outcome was plain agreement with the expert label. Results. The test comprised 25,091 units and 213,913 model calls. Jev's agreement with expert labels averaged 64.7% over six tasks. On 3,614 matched units it averaged 66.1%, against 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, and it was non-inferior to both on four of six tasks. Jev judged the whole pool in 17 minutes for US1.46; per judgment, it cost 1/34 of Sol's price and 1/152 of Opus's. A preset cutoff held its false-alarm rate on fresh planted-error answers, and in simulation, reviewing Jev's least-sure answers first found 1.4 times the errors of a random audit. Still, omissions were hard for both: at the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions and Opus 48.1%, and Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall. Conclusions. Across more than 200,000 model calls, a decision-only model was non-inferior to two frontier judges on most tasks at a small fraction of their cost and time, while reporting how sure it was of every call. With local cutoffs and expert oversight of omissions and clinical documents, judging every output of a deployed medical AI system becomes more affordable.

items.title: Deep learning grading of Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis from ultrasound images: a weighted soft-voting ensemble of convolutional and transformer networks
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Schistosomiasis morbidity still persists in China despite extensive progress towards elimination of new and active infections. Diagnosis of liver fibrosis related to Schistosoma japonicum remains challenging due to the subjective nature of ultrasound grading and the shortage of experienced sonographers in endemic counties. Methods: We developed a deep learning model that grades schistosomal liver fibrosis from a single B-mode ultrasound image without manual delineation of a region of interest. We used 2,921 images from 2,921 adults (aged 18-88 years, median age 54 years; 46.4% female) from a schistosomiasis hospital in Jiangxi Province, China, between 2019 and 2023. Of these, 12.9%, 34.6%, 32.4% and 20.2% had grade 0, 1, 2 and 3 fibrosis, respectively. Fibrosis grades were based on the clinical ultrasound record and re-evaluation by an experienced radiologist according to the Chinese Handbook of Schistosomiasis Control; discordant cases were reviewed by a second radiologist and resolved by consensus. Predictions from four neural networks with different architectures (ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet-121 and Swin-T) were combined by weighted soft voting, with weights derived from validation performance. Results: For the four-grade task this model achieved a macro-F1 of 0.8527 (95% CI 0.8184-0.8856), an accuracy of 0.8500 (0.8136-0.8818) and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.9187 (0.8983-0.9373) on a fixed test set of 440 images. For detecting significant fibrosis (grade 2 or 3; test-set prevalence 0.530), sensitivity was 0.9700, specificity was 0.9179, positive predictive value was 0.9300, negative predictive value was 0.9645, and AUROC was 0.9817. The ensemble achieved a higher macro-F1 than each individual backbone. Every ensemble misclassification was to an adjacent grade; no image with severe fibrosis was classified as no or mild fibrosis, or vice versa, whereas each individual backbone made 1-4 errors spanning two or more grades. Conclusions: The model may provide an automated aid for Schistosoma japonicum-associated fibrosis grading and could potentially support screening and follow-up in endemic areas after external validation.

items.title: Explainable Multimodal Prognostic Modeling Uncovers New Clinically Relevant Pathological Features in a Multi-Institutional Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Cohort
items.abstract_or_text: Although many patients with a well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PanNET) are cured after surgical resection, it is hard to predict outcome in these patients. Current prognostic assessment relies largely on Ki-67 proliferation index, tumor stage, and established adverse pathologic features, such as vascular and perineural invasion. However, individually, these variables incompletely explain why patients with similar clinicopathologic profiles sometimes experience markedly different outcomes. To address this challenge, we assembled three independent cohorts with a surgically resected PanNET. In total, we included 1,438 patients with approximately 30,000 histology images, and approximately 12,000 person-years of follow-up. We separately modeled structured clinicopathologic information with Cox regression and tumor-centered pathology images with deep learning on an internal cohort treated at Johns Hopkins Hospital and performed multimodal continuous-time survival modeling to reveal which clinical and pathologic features are most important in predicting patient outcome. Across Cox models of censored time to recurrence-free survival, a text-based clinicopathological model that incorporated known prognosticators achieved a C-index of approximately 0.87, the image-based histology model approximately 0.80, and decision-level late multimodal fusion approximately 0.88 on the internal test set. The clinical model demonstrated strong prognostic discrimination using established risk factors, mainly relying on the TNM stage and Ki-67 index. Primary tumor histology retained substantial prognostic signal, with analysis restricted to tumor-centered regions to reduce reliance on unrelated tissues that might indirectly indicate disease extent. Interpretation of high-attention image tiles revealed regions of importance in the primary tumor, including recognized adverse morphologic features such as the leading edge of the tumor and foci of vascular or perineural invasion. Unexpectedly, intratumoral and peritumoral stroma accounted for nearly 50% of the model's high-attention regions, suggesting that the stroma may yield equal prognostic information to neoplastic cells in recurrence-prediction models. To test generalizability, we further evaluated the trained models in independent cohorts from two institutions with different demographics, where discrimination varied by site (mean late-fusion C-indices of 0.864 and 0.723). Together with the improved discrimination achieved through late fusion, our findings suggest that current clinicopathologic variables can be modeled to form reliable prognosticators, and that routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained slides of the primary tumor contain additional prognostically important information not fully captured by conventional clinicopathologic assessment, such that together, the two sources provide complementary information.

items.title: Neural RNA splicing models rely on reading frame information unavailable to the splicing machinery
items.abstract_or_text: Deep neural networks can accurately predict RNA splice sites from genomic sequence, but whether they do so by simulating the natural splicing process is unclear. We evaluate this question by examining mutations that should not have a strong effect on splicing, but are correlated with it in the human genome. We focus specifically on mutations that affect frame alignment because this is known to be relevant to machinery that operates spatially and temporally separately from the splicing machinery. We find that predictions made by commonly-used neural tools are impacted far more by deletions or mutations that alter translational reading frame, producing in-frame stop codons, than by those that preserve reading frame. This dependence on reading frame causes these models to systematically miss many poison exons, a clinically relevant category of exons where reading frame is disrupted. This dependence is much weaker in "grey-box" models that build in splicing-specific structure. Our results imply that widely-used black-box models of splicing rely on information that is not accessible to the RNA splicing machinery. Code is available at https://github.com/kavigupta/frame-alignment-checks.

items.title: Comparative Transcriptomic Analysis of Gene Expression Patterns in Neutrophils from Rheumatoid Arthritis and COVID-19
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disorder characterised by chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, and neutrophils play a key role in its progression. COVID-19 also involves neutrophil hyperactivation that contributes to severe immune responses. Emerging evidence links COVID-19 to increased incidence or exacerbation of RA, potentially through overlapping immune mechanisms. Objective: To compare neutrophil transcriptomic profiles in RA and COVID-19 and identify shared immune pathways and disease-specific features. Methods: Publicly available neutrophil RNA-seq count data from the Gene Expression Omnibus were analysed: RA versus healthy controls (GSE116899) and COVID-19 versus healthy controls (GSE212041). A second COVID-19 comparison (severe versus convalescent) was assembled from GSE272381 and GSE227116. Differential expression was analysed with DESeq2, pathway enrichment with fgsea (Hallmark gene sets) and topGO (Gene Ontology biological process and molecular function). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were compared between diseases by direction of change. Results: In RA neutrophils, 11,355 DEGs were identified, of which 90 had an absolute log2 fold change of at least 2 with p<0.05 (70 upregulated, 20 downregulated). Twenty-four Hallmark gene sets were positively enriched at adjusted p<0.05, led by interferon alpha and interferon gamma responses, and Gene Ontology analysis highlighted type I interferon, antiviral and double-stranded RNA terms. In COVID-19 neutrophils, 420 DEGs were identified (37 upregulated, 383 downregulated), and no Hallmark gene set reached adjusted p<0.05. Of the 90 RA DEGs, 46 changed in the same direction in COVID-19 without reaching significance, and 27 changed significantly in the opposite direction, including CAMK1G, SIGLEC1, OAS1 and OAS3. In the second COVID-19 comparison, several of these genes, including OAS1, OAS3 and SIGLEC1, changed in the same direction as in RA. Conclusions: RA neutrophils show a transcriptional programme enriched for interferon and antiviral-response pathways. Part of the RA signature is shared with COVID-19 neutrophils, while a subset of genes diverges, and this divergence depended on the COVID-19 comparison used. These findings are hypothesis-generating and provide candidate genes for experimental validation.

items.title: VIGOR: Visual Gain Ordering for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion Language Models
items.abstract_or_text: Multimodal discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate responses through iterative mask prediction and offer a promising alternative to autoregressive large vision-language models. However, they still suffer from hallucination, producing outputs that are plausible under language priors but insufficiently grounded in the image. We argue that hallucination in multimodal dLLMs is not only a token prediction problem, but also a premature commitment problem: during iterative denoising, some masked positions are unmasked too early because their confidence is driven more by language priors than by visual evidence, and these early commitments can bias later generation. To address this issue, we propose Visual Gain Ordering (VIGOR), a training-free and plug-and-play inference strategy that reorders masked positions according to counterfactual visual evidence. At each denoising step, VIGOR compares the confidence of each candidate token under the original image-conditioned pass and an additional visual-ablation pass, and prioritizes positions whose predictions are more strongly supported by the image. Experiments on LLaDA-V and Lumina-DiMOO show that VIGOR consistently reduces hallucination and improves multimodal reasoning performance across benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/THU-BPM/Vigor.

items.title: Maternal diet and genetics shape the human milk metabolome
items.abstract_or_text: Human milk contains a diverse array of metabolites that contribute to infant nutrition, immune development, and microbial colonization. The maternal factors shaping the milk metabolome, and the relative contribution of genetics or diet vs. other factors, remain poorly understood. Here, we profiled 458 milk metabolites in 349 one-month postpartum human milk samples and integrated metabolomic data with maternal diet, clinical, transcriptomic, and genomic measurements. Maternal diet was broadly associated with milk metabolite composition, with significant correlations identified between dietary features and 323 metabolites. Coffee consumption strongly predicted milk quinic acid and 1,3-dimethyluric acid abundance, while high-fiber dietary patterns were associated with metabolites including proline-betaine and N-acetylornithine. Integration of milk transcriptomic and metabolomic data via machine learning identified biologically plausible gene-metabolite pairs, including associations between QPRT expression and quinolinic acid, and DPEP1 and cysteine-glycine dipeptide. Genome-wide association analyses identified nine study-wide significant metabolite quantitative trait loci, including novel milk-specific associations near PDE6A affecting purine metabolites and near GNE affecting free sialic acid. Comparison with plasma metabolite studies demonstrated both shared and milk-specific genetic regulation of metabolites. Finally, we found that of all tested maternal features, diet explained the largest proportion of variation in the milk metabolome. Together, these findings demonstrate that the human milk metabolome reflects both maternal exposures and mammary gland-specific biology. This work establishes a framework for understanding how genetic and environmental factors shape milk composition.

items.title: Preliminary Development of a Multimodal Deep Learning Model Integrating Clinical Data and Dual-Plane MRI to Predict 1-Year Patient-Reported Lower-Limb Numbness Improvement After Tubular Microdiscectomy
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Objective To develop and preliminarily evaluate a multimodal model integrating clinical data and dual-plane magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features to predict 1-year patient-reported lower-limb numbness improvement after tubular microdiscectomy (TMD). Materials and Methods This retrospective two-center study included 214 adults: 111 in the training cohort, 48 in the internal validation cohort, and 55 in the external validation cohort. Mean ages were 53.2 ± 15.0, 54.1 ± 14.1, and 51.4 ± 14.7 years, respectively; male participants comprised 58 (52.3%), 28 (58.3%), and 28 (50.9%), and female participants 53 (47.7%), 20 (41.7%), and 27 (49.1%), respectively. Deep features were extracted from sagittal and transverse T2-weighted MRI using residual networks and combined with clinical variables in a support vector machine. Outcome-informed feature selection and tuning were confined to the training cohort using 10-fold cross-validation. Candidate models and the decision threshold were selected using Hospital 1 internal validation data. ComBat parameters were estimated from Hospital 1 training data and applied to Hospital 2 without re-estimation; Hospital 2 did not inform model development. Results The final combined model incorporated 25 dual-plane MRI-derived features and four clinical variables. It yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.868 in the Hospital 1 internal validation cohort used for model selection and 0.833 (95% CI, 0.720–0.947) in the Hospital 2 external validation cohort. Comparisons with the clinical-only and dual-plane imaging-only models were descriptive and should be interpreted as exploratory. Conclusion This study provides preliminary model-development evidence that clinical and dual-plane MRI features may aid prediction of 1-year patient-reported numbness improvement after TMD. Larger prospective, multicenter, multivendor studies using validated sensory outcomes are needed before individualized clinical application.
